_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#5 — MAXITER: 1 is an ABORT, not an early exit, and it kills a linear deck whose residual has already converged. Five arms of one self-contained 3D HEX8 Statics deck (YOUNG 1000, NUE 0.3, surface Neumann, TOLDISP 1e-12 / TOLRES 1e-11), run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: MAXITER 1 exits 1 for BOTH kinematics settings with 'Failed.......Number of Iterations = 1 < 1' and 'The nonlinear solver did not converge!' from solver_nonlin_nox/4C_solver_nonlin_nox_problem.cpp line 165. The decisive part is that in that same Final Status Test block the residual test has PASSED — MAXITER1_RESIDUAL_TEST_PASSED=yes and MAXITER1_RESIDUAL_BELOW_TOL=yes (Structure-F-Norm 4.030e-16 < 1.000e-11) — while the iteration counter test failed, so 'one iteration is enough for a linear problem' is exactly backwards. MAXITER 2 on the identical deck exits 0 and finishes, and a generous cap costs nothing: MAXITER 2 and MAXITER 30 both spend 2 Newton iterations (GENEROUS_CAP_COSTS_EXTRA_ITERATIONS=no), the nonlinear deck 5, because Newton stops at the tolerance and not at the cap.
expect_in_output: The nonlinear solver did not converge!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the linear arm the cap that already suffices. The abort disappears, EXIT_LIN_MAXITER1 becomes 0 and the Final Status block no longer carries a failed iteration test, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the nonlinear arm the same way. EXIT_NLN_MAXITER1 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
